notes: Own.NET#266 slice 2, step 0. The VOCABULARY is frozen; no mapper exists.
The unit of analysis is one occurrence in revision A mapped to revision B.
pattern_id collides on purpose and occurrence_id cannot span runs, so lineage
is precisely the relation neither of those ids carries - and it is EARNED by
Absence of mapping evidence is 'unresolved', on EITHER side. It is not 'new',
not 'ended', and not the same lineage. Same invariant as finding-occurrence/v1
('identity is refused, not approximated') and as the runtime witness ('absence
of a record is not a semantic outcome').
revision_note: This contract was corrected before it was ever merged, under review of PR #65.
The first draft let 'ended' and 'new' be justified by no-mapping-evidence, and
gave 'unresolved' only an A-side anchor - so every unmatched B occurrence was
pushed toward 'new'. That is the fabricated-birth defect the contract exists to
forbid, written into the contract itself. It is fixed in place rather than as a
v2 because v1 has never been implemented or released: nothing is built on it.
Amended again by slice 2 STEP 1, which added 'conflicting-evidence'. Step 1
built a decision policy on this contract and found it had no way to say that
one observed structure supports two incompatible conclusions - a copy record
and a merge record touching one occurrence, which is N:M and therefore none of
the six outcomes. Step 1 first tried to report that as 'ambiguous-candidates',
which is a different thing: candidates are partners you cannot choose between,
not readings that contradict each other.
It was corrected here, in the senior contract, rather than by the junior one
inventing a value in a vocabulary it declares itself subordinate to. That the
junior contract had a written rule saying exactly this, and that the rule fired
on the very next review, is the reason it is written down at all.
Amended a third time by slice 2 STEP 1, which added
'insufficient-evidence-combination'. The step 1 fixture
`defeated-signal-drops-below-the-floor` leaves three evidence kinds standing
after a defeater removes a fourth - above this contract's floor of two - and
still licenses nothing, because no declared combination survives. The junior
contract first reported that as 'insufficient-evidence-kind', which was false
in the plain meaning of the words: the kinds were ample.
Corrected here rather than below, for the second review running. The junior
rule against widening from below has now fired twice, which is a better
argument for writing rules down than any amount of agreeing that one should.
Still frozen-unimplemented: no mapper exists, so nothing is built on the old
shape and nothing has to be migrated.
Amended a FOURTH time by slice 2 step 1, which added
'mutually_exclusive_evidence_kinds'. Step 1's per-rule coverage gate proved that
a rule reached by a fixture is still not a rule whose REQUIREMENTS are pinned:
swapping a continued rule's `line_drift` for `path_rename` left every check
green, because binding requirements to evidence is applicability and the step 1
suite deliberately refuses to compute it. Declaring which kinds cannot co-occur
closes part of that gap from the vocabulary side instead, where it costs no
second mapper. It does not close all of it - see the open question recorded in
the step 1 pull request.
Amended a FIFTH time by slice 2 step 1, which added
'evidence_kind_observation'. Step 1's kind-to-record map needed a value for
kinds that no record witnesses, and any such escape hatch can be pointed at a
kind that a record DOES witness. Which kinds those are is a fact about this
vocabulary rather than about any rule, so it is settled here and the junior map
is checked against it.

continued.means: exactly one successor, established by evidence

branched.forbids: picking a winner and discarding the rest; letting one successor inherit the predecessor's id, which is the same thing said with ids

merged.means: several predecessors collapse into one successor
merged.forbids: inheriting one predecessor's id - that is picking a winner among predecessors; and reporting the losing predecessors as 'ended', which reads as fixes that never happened

unresolved.means: the evidence does not decide - the DEFAULT when evidence is absent

sides.a: a predecessor in revision A whose successor was not established: names `frm`, leaves `to` empty
sides.b: an occurrence in revision B whose predecessor was not established: names `to`, leaves `frm` null

why_symmetric: Without the b side there is no way to say 'this occurrence in B is not
explained', and an unmatched B occurrence has nowhere to go but 'new'. The
schema would then manufacture the birth event the contract forbids - the
defect would be in the vocabulary, where no implementation could avoid it.

ended.means: no successor, and the absence is POSITIVELY evidenced
ended.note: an ending invents nothing. A predecessor already in a lineage has that lineage terminated; one that is not stays a positively evidenced terminal occurrence, without a pretended past. This is what keeps 'lineage' from inflating into 'every singleton must have an id'.
ended.forbids: an identity limitation as its justification - 'I found nothing' is unresolved, not a death

new.means: no predecessor, and the absence is POSITIVELY evidenced
new.note: an evidenced birth SEEDS a lineage: the occurrence gets a fresh root id with no incoming edge. Without it a later branch from this occurrence would have no parent lineage to record, and the only ways out are an empty parent, an occurrence id smuggled in as a lineage id, or a retroactive mint the contract never described.
new.forbids: an identity limitation as its justification - 'I found nothing' is unresolved, not a birth

same_pattern_id.why: pattern_id collides by design; two unrelated occurrences of one pattern share it

same_path.why: a file can hold several occurrences of the same pattern

path_rename.why: a rename relates files, not the occurrences inside them

structural_context.why: an enclosing symbol can hold several occurrences

anchored_content.why: identical content is exactly what cases 3 and 8 exploit

line_drift.why: proximity is not identity; case 8 is proximity without anything else

evidence_rule: No single evidence kind carries a 'continued' on its own.
Since every kind above is `sufficient_alone: false`, that floor is a COUNT:
a 'continued' names at least two kinds. `minimum_evidence_kinds_for_continued`
states it as data so the integrity suite can hold the fixtures to it - a floor
only written in prose is a floor a preregistered case can quietly sit under.
If a kind is ever promoted to `sufficient_alone: true`, that kind alone
satisfies the floor and the count stops applying to it.
This is a floor, not the algorithm: which COMBINATIONS suffice is slice 2
step 1 and is deliberately not fixed here.
Evidence is stored in its own field, never folded into the id and never
collapsed into a score that discards which signals fired.
limitations_rule: These say why a lineage_id is UNAVAILABLE. They belong to 'unresolved' and to
nothing else. An identity limitation is a statement about the mapper's reach;
'ended' and 'new' are statements about the world, and cannot be earned by one.
'no-predecessor-revision' means there is no revision A to compare against at
all - a first run. It must never be used while a predecessor revision exists.
'ambiguous-candidates' and 'conflicting-evidence' are neighbours and opposites,
and the difference is worth keeping sharp. Ambiguous candidates: SEVERAL
possible partners, nothing prefers one - the shape of two-candidates-unresolved.
Conflicting evidence: ONE observed structure that supports incompatible
conclusions about the same relation. The first is a choice with no grounds; the
second is grounds that argue with each other.
'insufficient-evidence-kind' and 'insufficient-evidence-combination' are the
second pair of neighbours, and the distinction is the whole reason
`minimum_evidence_kinds_for_continued` is called a floor.
Insufficient KIND: fewer kinds than the floor, or one kind carrying a mapping
no single kind may carry. The count is the problem.
Insufficient COMBINATION: the floor is met, sometimes comfortably, and no
combination a decision policy declares sufficient survives. Three kinds may be
present and the answer still unresolved, because two is the minimum a mapping
must clear and never the algorithm that decides which mappings are licensed.
Reporting the second as the first would say the evidence was too thin when it
was ample and simply did not add up to a rule anyone declared.

containing-file-deleted.why: the file that held the occurrence is gone, so no successor can exist in it
containing-file-deleted.defeated_why: a renamed file was not deleted; it moved, and the occurrence may have moved with it. A deleted path that is also a COPY SOURCE is the same story told in two records: the contents survive at the copy target, so the occurrence may survive with them, and reporting `ended` would announce a fix that a diff of the tree contradicts

containing-file-added.why: the file did not exist in revision A, so no predecessor could have lived in it
containing-file-added.defeated_why: a file that arrived as a copy or a rename has a SOURCE; its occurrences may descend from that source, which is the branch case, not a birth

enclosing-site-removed.why: the file survives but the site does not; the occurrence has nowhere left to be
enclosing-site-removed.defeated_why: a site folded into another was not removed but relocated; the merge record says where the occurrence went

enclosing-site-added.why: the site itself is new, so the occurrence in it cannot be a continuation
enclosing-site-added.defeated_why: a site that exists because other sites were folded into it inherits their occurrences; that is the merge case, not a birth

boundary_evidence_rule: 'ended' and 'new' are EARNED, exactly like 'continued' - the difference is only
that the evidence proves an edge of the lineage rather than a link in it.
Every kind names the machine-readable field it is read from, because a boundary
asserted in prose is not a boundary: the absence of an occurrence in revision B
is precisely what 'unresolved' already covers, so it can never be the evidence
The 'boundary:' prefix keeps these impossible to confuse with an identity
limitation in a stored record, which is how the first draft went wrong.
Each kind also names what DEFEATS it. Positive evidence that is explained away
by another record is not evidence: a deleted path that appears as a rename
source did not die, and an added path that appears as a copy target was not
born. Without the defeaters, 'the file is new' would license a birth for every
copied file, and the copy case and the birth case are the same shape.
lineage_id_existence: A lineage_id exists when MEMBERSHIP IN AN ESTABLISHED LINEAGE GRAPH is known.
Not 'when an edge was proven' - that earlier wording was tidier and wrong. It
made a root node unrepresentable, so an evidenced birth could not seed the
lineage a later branch would have to name as its parent.
'unresolved' establishes no membership and therefore seeds nothing, on either
side. That is the line the invariant actually has to hold.

lineage_id_rules.inherit: predecessor already carries a lineage_id -> the successor takes THAT id. A re-mint would read as a new defect appearing where an old one was proven to persist.
lineage_id_rules.mint: first proven 1:1 edge between two occurrences neither of which is linked yet -> mint once, and bind BOTH ends to it.
lineage_id_rules.branch: each successor gets its own fresh child id, and every child records parent_lineage_ids - LINEAGE ids, seeded first if the predecessor is unlinked. No successor inherits the predecessor's id, because inheriting is choosing.
lineage_id_rules.merge: the successor gets a freshly minted id which records parent_lineage_ids for EVERY predecessor, each of them a LINEAGE id, seeded first where needed. Inheriting one parent's id would silently elect it and orphan the rest.

lineage_id_rules_note: This is graph semantics, not an implementation detail, so it is fixed here
rather than left to the mapper. A mapper free to choose between inherit and
mint decides by itself whether a lineage survives reformatting, and a mapper
free to choose a merge id decides by itself which of several defects 'the'
surviving one is. Both are answers to questions this contract exists to ask.
What is still open is which evidence licenses each outcome - not what the ids

root_seeding_rules.unresolved: seeds nothing, on either side. A refusal that minted an id would make the refusal itself into membership.
root_seeding_rules.new: an evidenced birth mints a FRESH ROOT lineage id for its occurrence in revision B - a node with no incoming edge.
root_seeding_rules.continued: two unlinked occurrences: mint once and bind both. A linked predecessor: inherit.
root_seeding_rules.branched: an unlinked predecessor is seeded with a root lineage id FIRST; the children then get fresh child ids recording that lineage id.
root_seeding_rules.merged: every still-unlinked predecessor is seeded with its own root lineage id FIRST; the successor then gets a fresh id recording all of them.
root_seeding_rules.ended: mints nothing. A predecessor in a lineage has it terminated; an unlinked one stays a terminal occurrence, not a retroactive lineage of one.

root_seeding_note: new, branched and merged are the outcomes that build GRAPH STRUCTURE, and a
graph edge needs a node at both ends. Without seeding, a branch from an
occurrence born last revision has no parent lineage to name, and the only ways
out are an empty parent, an occurrence id smuggled in under a lineage field, or
a retroactive mint no rule describes. 'ended' is deliberately outside this: it
creates no structure, so requiring an id there would only inflate 'lineage'

parent_lineage_reference_forms.established: a literal lineage id the fixture already declares in revision_a.established_lineage
parent_lineage_reference_forms.seeded: lin-of:<occurrence_id> - THE LINEAGE OF that occurrence, seeded per root_seeding_rules if it has none yet

parent_lineage_rule: parent_lineage_ids holds LINEAGE ids. Never occurrence ids.
The distinction is the whole point of the three-way split at the top of this
contract: an occurrence_id cannot span runs by construction, so an occurrence
id stored in a lineage field is a cross-revision claim made out of something
Fixtures therefore write `lin-of:<occurrence_id>` rather than the bare id -
the reference is to the lineage, and it stays checkable that a lineage exists
for every predecessor without the fixture having to guess a minted value.
mapping_provenance_rule: A mapping is a statement about two specific runs over two specific revisions.
Recording both is what keeps it falsifiable outside the context that computed
it; 'mapper' is there because two mappers disagreeing about one pair of runs
is a fact worth being able to see.
A bare mapper name is not enough for that promise. Two runs of one name with
different thresholds are a disagreement that would look like a contradiction,
so the version, a digest of the configuration that was actually in force, and
the contract version the mapping was made under are all required. Without them
'would this mapping still be made under the new rule' has no answer.
preregistration_rule: Fixed BEFORE any algorithm exists, so the algorithm cannot select the cases
that flatter it. identity/tests/test_lineage_contract.py holds the matrix to
this list: a case removed or renamed fails the suite rather than disappearing.
Every one of the six outcomes must appear somewhere in the matrix, or that
outcome is frozen in name only and the mapper may implement it as it likes.

why: A path that is the SAME did not get renamed, and a path that got renamed
is not the same. These two kinds cannot both hold of one predecessor and
successor, and no rule in any junior contract may require both.
This is frozen here rather than in the decision policy because it is a fact
about the VOCABULARY, not about any particular rule that uses it. It was
added when slice 2 step 1 found that a continued rule could have its
`line_drift` requirement swapped for `path_rename` - producing a rule that
demands a file both stay put and move - with the whole integrity suite
green. Nothing in either contract said the combination was impossible, so
nothing could object.

mutually_exclusive_rule: A pair listed here is UNSATISFIABLE, so a rule requiring both is dead code that
no evidence can ever reach. That is a defect and not a conservative choice: a
rule which cannot fire silently removes the conclusion it was meant to license,
and the mapping degrades to `unresolved` while the contract still advertises the
rule. Junior contracts are checked against this list; they may not add to it from
below, for the same reason they may not widen `limitations` from below.

why: HOW EACH KIND IS OBSERVED, which decides whether anything in revision B has
to be produced to support a claim about it.
A `pair_property` is read off the two occurrences themselves: `same_path`
compares two paths, `anchored_content` two strings. Nothing in the diff
witnesses it and nothing can be checked against a record.
A `revision_record` is not visible in the pair at all. Two occurrences at
different paths look identical whether the file MOVED or whether one ended and
another began; only a record in revision B distinguishes them. That is the
whole of the absence-of-record doctrine at the evidence layer, and it is why
`path_rename` is the one kind a junior contract must bind to a record.
Frozen here, above the decision policy, because a junior contract listing its
own record-less kinds could declare `path_rename` record-less and unbind the
rename rule while every check on the mapping still passed. That mutation was
green until this section existed.
